# Pan-Tilt-Controller: Keyboard input to serial motor commands

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/pan-tilt-controller/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/pan-tilt-controller/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/Pan-Tilt-Controller
- Inspected revision: b565efdf9d3fc83096d18c667b6d7a7e21383377

## Summary

This archived pan-tilt controller connects a desktop interface to a serial-controlled positioning unit. The implementation mixes a Qt event loop with pyserial commands and keeps the requested pan and tilt positions in global state.

**Why it exists:** Serial interface and motion control daemon for Directed Perception PTU-46 precision pan-tilt robotic camera units.

**Best fit:** Automated camera positioning for computer vision experiments.

## Use cases

Python 2 desktop and command-line tools that drive a PTU-46-17.5 pan-tilt unit over a serial port.

- **Initialize the unit on start** (PTU-46-17.5 unit): On start, pantiltcontroller.py opens COM3 at 9600 baud and sends speed, acceleration, reset, home position and pan and tilt limit commands (pxu1500, pnu-1000, tnu-850, txu585).
- **Move to a pan/tilt position** (Lab operator, PTU-46-17.5 unit): The PyQt5 window in pantiltcontroller.py has Pan and Tilt fields; OK sends pp&lt;value&gt; and tp&lt;value&gt; and shows the unit&#39;s reply in a log box.
- **Jog with arrows or buttons** (Lab operator, PTU-46-17.5 unit): The Control menu (Ctrl&#43;O) opens a dialog whose arrow buttons, and the keyboard arrow keys, move pan or tilt by 5 positions per press.
- **Return to home position** (Lab operator, PTU-46-17.5 unit): The Reset button sends pp0 and tp0 and sets the stored positions back to zero.
- **Send raw serial commands** (Lab operator, PTU-46-17.5 unit): PTC-command.py is a prompt that forwards each typed line (for example r, pnu 1000, pp0) to the unit and prints the reply until exit is typed.

### Scenario: Point the pan-tilt unit at a target

1. Connect the PTU-46-17.5 to COM3 (the port is hard-coded) on a Windows PC with Python 2.7, pyserial, PyQt5 and pywin32.
2. Run python pantiltcontroller.py; the script sets limits and moves the unit to 0,0.
3. Type 500 in Pan and -200 in Tilt, then click OK.
4. Open Control, Control and fine-tune with the arrow keys in steps of 5.
5. Click Reset to bring the unit back to home.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| Python | 100 |

## Features and components

- **Interface events** — pantiltcontroller.py imports PyQt5 and installs a key event filter. Arrow keys and buttons adjust a position variable, then build a pp or tp command. This differs from the older framework description in the README.
- **Device initialization** — The module opens COM3 at 9600 baud and writes initialization commands at import time. The UI therefore has an immediate hardware dependency, before a user selects a port or confirms movement.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Qt key or button event → Requested position state
- Requested position state → Serial command string
- Serial command string → pyserial connection
- pyserial connection → Pan-tilt hardware

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;Qt key or button event&#34;]
  n1[&#34;Requested position state&#34;]
  n2[&#34;Serial command string&#34;]
  n3[&#34;pyserial connection&#34;]
  n4[&#34;Pan-tilt hardware&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n2 --&gt; n3
  n3 --&gt; n4
```

**One path through the code:** Follow one arrow-key branch from positionPan or positionTilt to ser.write. The variable records the command target, not independently measured physical position.

## Constraints and checks

Do not import or run this script against attached hardware without reviewing startup motion, travel limits and emergency-stop behavior. It also uses Python 2-era syntax.

## Files to read

- [pantiltcontroller.py](https://github.com/antoinebou12/Pan-Tilt-Controller/blob/master/pantiltcontroller.py)
- [PTC-command.py](https://github.com/antoinebou12/Pan-Tilt-Controller/blob/master/PTC-command.py)
- [README.md](https://github.com/antoinebou12/Pan-Tilt-Controller/blob/master/README.md)

# PolyFEMBlenderPlugin: PolyFEM simulations from a Blender scene

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/polyfemblenderplugin/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/polyfemblenderplugin/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/ETSim/PolyFEMBlenderPlugin
- Inspected revision: 70794d3107843eeaa55210ff899d1f86a9ba5cf5


## Use cases

Blender add-on that turns a scene into a PolyFEM JSON setup and runs the simulation from Blender.

- **Assign FEM materials** (Simulation user): The Apply Material operator stores Young&#39;s modulus, Poisson&#39;s ratio and density on the selected objects from a preset list such as Steel or Aluminum.
- **Create PolyFEM JSON** (Simulation user): Create PolyFEM JSON exports each mesh and writes geometry, materials, contact, time, boundary-condition, solver and output blocks to one JSON file.
- **Tetrahedralize with TetWild** (Simulation user, Docker images): With the MSH export type, the object is written as STL and converted to .msh by the yixinhu/tetwild image or a local TetWild executable.
- **Run the simulation** (Simulation user, Docker images, PolyFEM solver): Run PolyFem Simulation calls docker run antoinebou12/polyfem --json with the project folder mounted on /data, or a local PolyFEM executable, in a background thread.
- **Import results as animation** (Simulation user, PolyFEM solver): Render Animation reads step_*.vtu files, adds the solution displacement, converts each step to OBJ with meshio and keyframes its visibility.
- **Pull solver images** (Simulation user, Docker images): The Pull Docker Image buttons check that Docker is installed and run docker pull for the configured TetWild or PolyFEM image.

### Scenario: Simulate a contact scene and play it back in Blender

1. Install the zipped polyfem folder through Edit &gt; Preferences &gt; Add-ons and enable PolyFem.
2. In Properties &gt; Physics &gt; PolyFEM, choose Docker execution and pull antoinebou12/polyfem and yixinhu/tetwild.
3. Select the meshes, apply a material preset and set contact, time step and end time.
4. Click Create JSON Configuration to write the meshes and the JSON file to the export path.
5. Click Run PolyFem Simulation, then Render Animation to import the step_*.vtu results as keyframed meshes.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| Python | 100 |

# RawAnalyser: From raw sensor values to diagnostic plots

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/rawanalyser/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/rawanalyser/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/RawAnalyser
- Inspected revision: ff745802fe293ebba44bf54389509dbb95d0fe5f

## Summary

RawAnalyser is an older Python image-analysis experiment for clipping, channel values, gamma and vignetting. Its input assumptions are visible in the implementation, including a fixed raw frame shape and regions selected through a JSON file.

**Why it exists:** Sensor pixel analysis tool computing clipping histograms and dynamic range for RAW camera frames.

**Best fit:** Camera sensor benchmarking and exposure verification in computational photography.

## Use cases

Python 2 scripts for camera-tuning engineers to check clipping, gamma and vignetting in raw Bayer sensor captures.

- **Mark ROI and gray patches** (Image quality engineer): GUI.py (PyQt5) opens a .raw or .tiff file, converts raw to TIFF for display and saves the clicked region of interest and gray patch corners to json/points.json.
- **Analyse each new raw capture** (Image quality engineer, Camera capture folder): RawAnalyser.py uses a watchdog observer on the given folder; every new 1928 x 1088 16-bit raw file is split into Bayer channels, saved as TIFF and analysed.
- **Detect black or white clipping** (Image quality engineer): clipping() prints per-channel minimum and maximum 10-bit levels and flags CLIPPING BLACK or white in colour when values reach the sensor limits.
- **Measure gamma and vignetting** (Image quality engineer): gamma() samples the gray patches from points.json; vignette() subtracts the black level (--bl, default 1024), divides by a stored .npy vignette map and writes a corrected TIFF.
- **Inspect one pixel&#39;s value** (Image quality engineer): RawPixel.py prints the value and Bayer colour of the pixel at x, y for a given width, height and bit depth, and dumps channels to array/*.txt.
- **Convert raw files to TIFF** (Image quality engineer, Camera capture folder): Raw2Tiff.py writes a TIFF from one raw file; 20MPto5MP.py bins 20 MP OV20880 frames by summing 2 x 2 same-colour pixels into a 5 MP image.

### Scenario: Check an OV2740 colour-checker capture

1. Install Python 2.7 and the packages in requirements.txt, plus tifffile.
2. Run python GUI.py, open a capture from raw/ and click the ROI and gray patches to update json/points.json.
3. Start python RawAnalyser.py raw json/points.json --func basic --bl 1024 to watch the folder.
4. Copy a new .raw capture into raw/; the script prints clipping warnings and gamma figures and writes a TIFF under tiff/.
5. Check a suspicious spot with python RawPixel.py &lt;file&gt; x y --width 1928 --height 1088.

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| Python | 100 |



### README.md · Usage

```bash

```


## Features and components

- **File watcher and raw layout** — NewAnalyse reacts to file creation, loads region coordinates and reads uint16 data. The code reshapes the array to 1088 by 1928 pixels and writes a TIFF. Those dimensions are part of the implementation, not inferred from the file.
- **Regions and channels** — The analysis builds crop and gray-reference matrices before separating channel samples with fixed index patterns. Plots and statistics therefore depend on both the region file and the assumed sensor layout.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Raw frame and region JSON → Watchdog event
- Watchdog event → uint16 array and reshape
- uint16 array and reshape → Region and channel extraction
- Region and channel extraction → TIFF and diagnostic plots

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;Raw frame and region JSON&#34;]
  n1[&#34;Watchdog event&#34;]
  n2[&#34;uint16 array and reshape&#34;]
  n3[&#34;Region and channel extraction&#34;]
  n4[&#34;TIFF and diagnostic plots&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n2 --&gt; n3
  n3 --&gt; n4
```

**One path through the code:** Follow np.fromfile into reshape, then compare the crop bounds with the channel loops. A plausible-looking plot can still be wrong if the input dimensions or Bayer layout differ from those fixed assumptions.

## Constraints and checks

Python 2 syntax and deprecated scientific-library calls make this historical code. It is not a general RAW decoder or a validated camera-calibration package.

# retroarch-web-games: Packaging an emulator for a static web server

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/retroarch-web-games/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/retroarch-web-games/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/retroarch-web-games
- License: MIT
- Inspected revision: 71b41f91e252873023336b14d4582aa1ac5e2b44

## Summary

retroarch-web-games is an archived container setup around a web build of RetroArch. The repository combines browser runtime files with scripts and container assembly. Hosting the player and supplying game content are separate concerns.

**Why it exists:** Containerized WebAssembly RetroArch emulator bundle ready to run in any browser with zero installation.

**Best fit:** Zero-friction retro gaming via Docker on desktop, mobile, or smart TVs.

## Use cases

Docker image that self-hosts the RetroArch web player behind nginx, with game folders fetched at build time.

- **Install RetroArch web build** (Self-hoster, Online file sources): setup_retroarch.sh downloads the previous day&#39;s emscripten build from buildbot.libretro.com, extracts it into /var/www/html and unpacks the frontend bundle.
- **Download game sets** (Self-hoster, Online file sources): InternetArchive.py (typer, rich, requests) scrapes the listed archive pages for .zip and .7z files in parallel and saves them under downloads/&lt;system name&gt;.
- **Sort games by first letter** (Self-hoster): sort_mkdir.sh moves each file into a 0-9 or A-Z subfolder; the Dockerfile runs it for every Nintendo system folder.
- **Run the container** (Self-hoster): docker-compose up -d builds the image and maps port 8080 to nginx; entrypoint.sh regenerates the .index-xhr file lists before starting nginx.
- **Play in the browser** (Browser player): The player opens http://localhost:8080, picks a core and loads a game in the RetroArch Web Player page shipped with the nightly build (the repository keeps a copy as index.html, not copied by the Dockerfile).
- **Publish multi-arch images** (Self-hoster): .github/workflows/retroarch-web-games.yaml builds with Docker Buildx for amd64, arm64 and arm/v7 and pushes antoinebou12/retroarch-web-games to Docker Hub.

### Scenario: Host a retro game player on a home server

1. Clone the repository and check there is room for an image of about 10 GB, as the README warns.
2. Run docker-compose up -d; the build runs setup_retroarch.sh, InternetArchive.py and sort_mkdir.sh.
3. When the container starts, entrypoint.sh indexes the cores and bundle, then nginx serves the site.
4. Open http://localhost:8080 and load a game from the sorted downloads folders.



## Features and components

- **Container assembly** — The Dockerfile prepares the web-serving environment and installation material. entrypoint.sh controls container startup, while index.html and libretro.js belong to the browser-facing runtime.
- **Runtime and content** — The browser loads the emulator runtime and its associated assets. Game files must match the expected core and format. Repository download scripts describe content acquisition separately from running the web interface.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Docker build → Static server files
- Static server files → Browser emulator runtime
- User-provided game content → Browser emulator runtime

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;Docker build&#34;]
  n1[&#34;Static server files&#34;]
  n2[&#34;Browser emulator runtime&#34;]
  n3[&#34;User-provided game content&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n3 --&gt; n2
```

**One path through the code:** Read the Dockerfile alongside entrypoint.sh to separate image-build downloads from runtime serving. An image that builds successfully may still lack a browser-compatible core or the assets needed by a selected game.

## Constraints and checks

This archived setup needs dependency and browser review before reuse. Only use game content you are entitled to use; no game downloads are needed to inspect the architecture.

# Salary: exploring Canadian salary guides and wage data

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/salary/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/salary/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/AlgoETS/Salary
- Inspected revision: 40b10f4d6a2a6670400b960c2476d9b7e494eaa1


## Use cases

Python scripts and notebooks that extract Canadian salary guides and wage tables to compare jobs by region.

- **Extract salary guide PDFs** (Salary analyst): src/pdf_salary_scraper_2023_1.py and src/pdf_salary_scraper_2024_1.py read a guide in data/pdf with PyPDF2, track province and region, parse entry, mid and senior ranges per job and save a pickle in data/pickle.
- **Load 2012–2022 wage tables** (Salary analyst): src/wages_in_time.py reads data/csv/wage_2012.csv to wage_2022.csv with Polars, harmonizes column names, caches data/pickle/wages.pkl and prints the top-paid jobs per year and engineering jobs per province.
- **Compare jobs by region** (Salary analyst): sandbox/salary_exploration_2023.ipynb and salary_exploration_2024.ipynb rank jobs by maximum salary, filter engineering and Québec jobs, compare one job across regions and provinces, and find the widest gaps.
- **Scrape Stack Overflow pay** (Salary analyst, Stack Overflow survey): src/stackoverflow_scraper.py fetches the 2022 Stack Overflow survey salary page with httpx, parses the table with BeautifulSoup and pickles it to data/pickle/stackoverflow_salary_data.pkl.
- **Query salary data over HTTP** (API client): api/app.py is a FastAPI app whose /load_pickle/2023 and /salary/2024 routes return the pickled guides as JSON; interactive documentation is at /docs.

### Scenario: Compare cloud architect pay across Québec regions

1. Run pip install -r requirements.txt from the repository root.
2. Place 2023_salary_guide.pdf in data/pdf and run python src/pdf_salary_scraper_2023_1.py.
3. Check that data/pickle/salary_guide_2023.pkl was written.
4. Start jupyter notebook and open sandbox/salary_exploration_2023.ipynb, which splits each range and computes entry, mid and senior means.
5. Call compare_job_province(&#39;cloud architect&#39;, &#39;québec&#39;) to rank Québec regions by mean mid-level salary.

# Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK: Adapting log events to Sentry

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/serilog-sinks-sentrysdk/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/serilog-sinks-sentrysdk/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK
- License: MIT
- Inspected revision: d0b5c252b942f61f097feccef10ac2d2b43aad7b

## Summary

Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK connects a .NET logging pipeline to the Sentry SDK. Its sink converts structured log events for Sentry, so application call sites can keep using Serilog.

**Why it exists:** Production .NET 6&#43; Serilog sink bridging structured logging and Sentry error telemetry with zero allocation overhead.

**Best fit:** Enterprise .NET microservice error observability and distributed trace correlation.

## Use cases

NuGet Serilog sink for .NET developers that sends logs, exceptions and traces to Sentry, with ASP.NET Core context.

- **Configure WriteTo.Sentry** (.NET developer): SentrySinkExtensions.cs adds WriteTo.Sentry with a DSN and options such as environment, release, sampleRate, tags and enableTracing, usable from code or the Serilog section of appsettings.json.
- **Send logs and exceptions** (.NET developer, Sentry): SentrySink.Emit maps the Serilog level, copies properties into scope extras and tags, adds breadcrumbs and calls CaptureMessage or CaptureException.
- **Trace each log as a span** (.NET developer, Sentry): With enableTracing on, Emit starts a transaction named from the message template and a child span through ITransactionService, then finishes both.
- **Attach HTTP request context** (.NET developer, Sentry): The AspNetCore package adds app.AddSentryContext() middleware and HttpContextDestructingPolicy so events carry the user, headers and request data.
- **Scrub data before sending** (.NET developer): An optional beforeSend callback is chained after the sink&#39;s own handling; the SentryWeb demo also rewrites messages with a Serilog enricher (Scrubbing/DivisionByZeroFilter.cs).
- **Publish six NuGet packages** (NuGet.org): .github/workflows/CI.yml packs the main, .6 and .10 package ids for net6.0 and net10.0 and pushes them to NuGet.org when a GitHub release is published.

### Scenario: Report errors from an ASP.NET Core app to Sentry

1. Run dotnet add package Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK and dotnet add package Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK.AspNetCore.
2. Put the project DSN under Serilog, WriteTo, Sentry, Args in appsettings.json.
3. Build the logger with ReadFrom.Configuration, Destructure.With&lt;HttpContextDestructingPolicy&gt;() and the CheckIfCaptured filter.
4. Call app.AddSentryContext() in Startup.Configure.
5. Trigger an error, for example with dotnet run --project demos/SentryWeb/SentryWeb.csproj, and find the event with its request data in Sentry.

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| C# | 98.04 |
| PowerShell | 1.96 |

## Features and components

- **Sink and SDK boundary** — SentrySink.cs defines an SDK wrapper interface with capture-message, capture-exception and transaction methods. The wrapper delegates to SentrySdk. This boundary gives tests a substitute for the external SDK calls.
- **Application context** — The source tree separates the sink package from ASP.NET Core integration and tests. Request and user factories adapt HTTP context. Logging configuration and request enrichment therefore have different responsibilities.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Application log event → Serilog pipeline
- Serilog pipeline → Sentry sink and context
- Sentry sink and context → SDK wrapper
- SDK wrapper → Sentry SDK

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;Application log event&#34;]
  n1[&#34;Serilog pipeline&#34;]
  n2[&#34;Sentry sink and context&#34;]
  n3[&#34;SDK wrapper&#34;]
  n4[&#34;Sentry SDK&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n2 --&gt; n3
  n3 --&gt; n4
```

**One path through the code:** Follow an exception-bearing log through the sink and compare it with a message-only event. The wrapper exposes separate capture operations, so a useful test checks the chosen operation and its event data, not only that a call occurred.

## Constraints and checks

Request context can contain personal data. Review enrichment and filtering before forwarding it; package presence alone does not establish a privacy policy.

- [src/Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK/AspNetCoreSentryRequestFactory.cs](https://github.com/antoinebou12/Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK/blob/main/src/Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK/AspNetCoreSentryRequestFactory.cs)

# SimilityVectorEmbedding: movie similarity with vector search

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/similityvectorembedding/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/similityvectorembedding/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/AlgoETS/SimilityVectorEmbedding
- Inspected revision: f3db0326f06dcadc56e0809fa054135f0ecacfc5


## Use cases

Jupyter notebooks that embed a movie catalog and find similar films with pgvector, Qdrant, BM25, Neo4j and Ollama.

- **Embed the movie catalog** (Learner, Database container): postgres/1.create_table.ipynb builds one text per film from movies.json and encodes it with BART, GTE, MiniLM-L12, RoBERTa and e5-large, storing one vector column per model.
- **Find films like a title** (Learner, Database container): postgres/0.simple.ipynb resolves the typed title with pg_trgm, then ranks the catalog by cosine similarity for one title, several titles or rated titles.
- **Search from a Gradio page** (Learner, Database container): The last cells of postgres/0.simple.ipynb launch a Gradio interface with Single, Multiple and Ratings modes that shows posters, years and similarity scores.
- **Search with Qdrant** (Learner, Database container): qdrant/0.simple.ipynb upserts 384-dimension MiniLM vectors into a cosine collection, searches it and projects the vectors with t-SNE and k-means.
- **Ask a local LLM** (Learner, Database container, Local LLM (Ollama)): postgres/3.LLMS.ipynb embeds a question, runs a pgvector cosine query and passes the schema to a LangChain chain backed by Ollama llama2:13b-chat.
- **Compare BM25 and graph search** (Learner, Database container): bm25/0.bm25.ipynb ranks films by keywords with rank_bm25, and neo4j/1.create_db.ipynb scores films by shared genres, directors, writers and actors.

### Scenario: Find films like The Matrix

1. Start PostgreSQL with pgvector and pg_trgm: cd postgres, then docker-compose up -d.
2. Open postgres/0.simple.ipynb with jupyter notebook and run the pip install and import cells.
3. Run main() to load movies.json, embed each film with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and insert it into the movies table.
4. Call find_similar_movies(conn, cur, &#34;The Matrix&#34;) to get the closest titles above a 0.5 cosine threshold.
5. Plot the result with plot_similar_movies or try the same search in the Gradio interface.

# Simulateur: a Django stock-market simulation game

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/simulateur/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/simulateur/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/AlgoETS/Simulateur
- Inspected revision: 77f9e70c9982784327ac522c6dc6fcd050ad2ffc


## Use cases

Django stock-market game where admins run scripted scenarios and teams trade simulated stocks live.

- **Build a scenario** (Simulation admin): The admin dashboard walks through five form steps (settings, companies and stocks, teams, events, review) backed by the scenario and simulation-manager APIs.
- **Run a market simulation** (Simulation admin): manage.py start_simulation sets a simulation to ongoing; SimulationManager then writes OHLC candles from the chosen noise model (Brownian, Perlin, random walk, fBm, Monte Carlo) at each time step.
- **Generate content with AI** (Simulation admin, Ollama LLM): simulation/api/ai_llm.py exposes create-news-ai, create-event-ai, create-trigger-ai, create-company-stock-ai and create-scenario-ai, which prompt an Ollama model (OLLAMA_MODEL, llama3 by default).
- **Join a team** (Player): A team member generates a join link from the team dashboard (team/generate-join-link/) and other players join with it; the same page shows members and leaderboards.
- **Buy and sell stocks** (Player): From /dashboard/, the order form calls POST /api/stock/buy/ or /api/stock/sell/, which check the balance against the latest price, record an order and update holdings.
- **Follow live prices** (Player): The game dashboard opens ws/simulation/&lt;id&gt;/ and Django Channels pushes stock updates, news, events and triggers from SimulationConsumer.

### Scenario: Run the seeded demo simulation

1. In simulateur/, copy env-default to .env and run python3 run.py --install to install packages, migrate, create admin/admin and seed the CSV data.
2. Start the ASGI server and simulation 1 with python3 run.py --start-simulation 1 (Daphne on port 8000).
3. Sign in as admin and open /dashboard/admin to review the scenario, settings and noise function.
4. Open /dashboard/game: candles arrive over the ws/simulation/ WebSocket at each timer step.
5. From /dashboard/, choose the simulation and a stock and press Buy, which calls POST /api/stock/buy/; then check holdings and leaderboards.

# sm64coopdx-switch-N3DS: Keeping a port behind platform interfaces

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/sm64coopdx-switch-n3ds/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/sm64coopdx-switch-n3ds/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/sm64coopdx-switch-N3DS
- Inspected revision: 567fd71a962d44e006461f3085a3a7ca3a063eb4

## Summary

This fork explores Switch and New 3DS targets for sm64coopdx. Shared game and co-op code sit above platform-specific graphics, audio and input. The platform probe is a smaller executable with a narrower purpose than the full game.

**Why it exists:** Low-level C systems port optimizing multi-threaded networking and memory layout for embedded handheld consoles.

**Best fit:** Co-op multiplayer emulation and custom embedded gaming on Switch &amp; N3DS.

## Use cases

Unofficial Nintendo Switch homebrew port of sm64coopdx online co-op, with an early New 3DS target; you supply the ROM.

- **Install with your own ROM** (Switch player): docs/SWITCH_INSTALL.md: extract the release ZIP to the SD card root, add a US ROM as switch/sm64coopdx/baserom.us.z64 matching sm64.us.sha1, and launch sm64coopdx.nro in full application mode.
- **Join a public CoopNet lobby** (Switch player, CoopNet lobby service): The Switch build sends its genuine NRO fingerprint and lists lobbies in the sm64coop-android namespace, as described in docs/switch.md; the client code is under src/pc/network/coopnet.
- **Play over local wireless** (Switch player): src/pc/network/socket/socket_ldn.c adds a local wireless transport and src/pc/djui/djui_panel_ldn_browser.c lists nearby sessions.
- **Enter a lobby password** (Switch player, CoopNet lobby service): Private-lobby passwords use the in-game keypad in src/pc/djui/djui_panel_switch_text_entry.c instead of the native Switch keyboard.
- **Build and package the NRO** (Port developer): In the devkitpro/devkita64 Docker image, make -f Makefile.switch-sdmc SWITCH_COOPNET=1 switch-nro builds the NRO and switch-dist checks the header and hashes and writes the release ZIP; build-switch-game.yml runs ROM-free portability gates in CI.
- **Build the New 3DS target** (Port developer): Makefile.new3ds builds a platform shell and Makefile.new3ds-game the full engine with a Citro3D renderer and NDSP audio; docs/new3ds-port.md says gameplay on hardware is not verified yet.

### Scenario: Play co-op online from a Switch

1. Extract the sm64coopdx Switch release ZIP to the SD card root, creating switch/sm64coopdx/.
2. Copy your own US ROM to switch/sm64coopdx/baserom.us.z64.
3. Hold R while starting a game to open the Homebrew Menu in full application mode, then launch SM64CoopDX.
4. Open the join menu, pick a public CoopNet lobby and type its password on the in-game keypad if it is private.
5. If something fails, read startup.log, coopnet.log and exception.log under switch/sm64coopdx/logs/.

## Features and components

- **Shared runtime and backends** — src/pc separates controller, audio, graphics, networking and platform code. Porting work can replace a backend while keeping shared game behavior. Build flags and target makefiles determine which implementations are linked.
- **The platform probe** — Makefile.switch-platform compiles a probe with Switch lifecycle, input and crash-log code, then packages an NRO using devkitPro tools. Its source list is deliberately smaller than the full game’s build.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Shared game and co-op code → Platform interfaces
- Platform interfaces → Graphics backend
- Platform interfaces → Controller and audio backends
- Graphics backend → Console runtime
- Controller and audio backends → Console runtime

```mermaid
flowchart LR
```

**One path through the code:** Read the probe’s SOURCES list before interpreting a successful build. It exercises selected platform modules; it does not establish that every game subsystem, graphics path or co-op session works on the console.

## Constraints and checks

# Sport-Arbitrage: a sports-betting arbitrage calculator

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/sport-arbitrage/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/sport-arbitrage/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/AlgoETS/Sport-Arbitrage
- Inspected revision: dbee18848ac988cd6f99764c3148d5e3349035b2


## Use cases

Browser calculator that checks two bookmakers&#39; odds for a sports-betting arbitrage and splits the stake.

- **Pick 2 or 3 outcomes** (Bettor): The Number of Odds selector in index.html calls toggleOddsFields() in script.js, which shows the two Draw fields only for three outcomes.
- **Enter odds from two sites** (Bettor): The form takes Win and Lost odds for Site 1 and Site 2, optional Draw odds, and the total investment.
- **Detect an arbitrage** (Bettor): calculateArbitrage() tests fixed cross-site pairings; hasArbitrageOpportunity() reports one when the sum of inverse odds is below 1.
- **Split the stake** (Bettor): For each opportunity, script.js prints the arbitrage percentage, optimal stakes, returns per outcome and guaranteed profit.
- **Check the math in Python** (Bettor): arbitrage.ipynb implements the same functions in Python with hard-coded sample odds for the two-outcome case.

### Scenario: Test the notebook&#39;s sample odds

1. Open index.html in a browser and keep Number of Odds at 2.
2. Enter Win Site 1 = 1.3, Lost Site 1 = 3.93, Win Site 2 = 1.42 and Lost Site 2 = 2.9.
3. Enter a Total Investment of 100 and click Calculate.
4. Read the result: only the lost-site1 and win-site2 pair qualifies, with stakes of about 26.54 and 73.46.
5. Compare with the guaranteed profit line (about 4.31) and rerun arbitrage.ipynb to check the same numbers.

| --- | ---: |
| JavaScript | 38.34 |
| Jupyter Notebook | 33.46 |
| HTML | 25.5 |

# SpringBootFilesUploader: file uploads, and a small server console

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/springbootfilesuploader/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/springbootfilesuploader/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/SpringBootFilesUploader
- License: MIT
- Inspected revision: 3be3bbc6d828edf840ab6edaffee661db671d7db

## Summary

SpringBootFilesUploader is a Kotlin and Spring backend with a file-upload path that separates binary storage from document metadata. A file identifier returned to the client connects those two representations during download.

**Why it exists:** Spring Boot microservice written in Kotlin with streaming multipart file upload and integrity validation.

**Best fit:** High-throughput file ingestion and storage backend.

## Use cases

Kotlin Spring Boot API that stores uploaded files in MinIO/S3 behind JWT roles, with Docker and SSH admin endpoints.

- **Sign up and get a JWT** (API user, MinIO S3 and MongoDB): POST /auth/signup saves a user with hashed password and roles in MongoDB; POST /auth/signin returns a JwtResponse with the token and roles (AuthController.kt, JwtUtils.kt).
- **Upload a document** (Moderator or admin, MinIO S3 and MongoDB): POST /files/documents (moderator or admin) checks the extension against DOC_FILE_EXTENSION_REGEX, writes the bytes to the S3 bucket under files/&lt;uuid&gt;/&lt;name&gt; and records metadata in MongoDB.
- **Download a stored file** (API user, MinIO S3 and MongoDB): GET /files/{id} looks up the file record in MongoDB, reads the object from S3 and returns it as an attachment with its content type and size.
- **Manage Docker containers** (Moderator or admin): The /containers routes list, create, start, stop, restart and rename containers through docker-java against the Docker host set in application.yml (tcp://127.0.0.1:2375).
- **Run a remote SSH command** (Moderator or admin): POST /ssh/cli (admin only) opens an Apache SSHD session with the host, port and credentials in the request body and returns the command output.

### Scenario: Store a PDF and fetch it back

1. Start MongoDB on localhost:27017 and MinIO on localhost:9000, as configured in application.yml, then run ./gradlew bootRun.
2. POST /auth/signup with a username, email, password and the role &#34;mod&#34;.
3. POST /auth/signin and copy the JWT from the response.
4. POST /files/documents with the PDF in the multipart field &#34;document&#34; and the Bearer token; the response returns fileId and fileName.
5. GET /files/{fileId} to download the PDF, or browse the routes in Swagger UI at /api-docs.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| Kotlin | 99.52 |
| Java | 0.31 |
| Dockerfile | 0.17 |

## Features and components

- **HTTP validation** — FilesController accepts a multipart document, checks its filename extension and declares moderator/admin upload roles. The size-check block is commented out. Downloads use a file ID and return stored content type and length.
- **Storage coordination** — FilesService creates a UUID-based path and sends bytes to FileRepository. It then saves a FileModel through FilesMongo. Reads look up the metadata first, then use its path to retrieve the bytes.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Multipart upload → FilesController
- FilesController → FilesService
- FilesService → FileRepository binary storage
- FilesService → FilesMongo metadata
- FilesMongo metadata → File ID response

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;Multipart upload&#34;]
  n1[&#34;FilesController&#34;]
  n2[&#34;FilesService&#34;]
  n3[&#34;FileRepository binary storage&#34;]
  n4[&#34;FilesMongo metadata&#34;]
  n5[&#34;File ID response&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n2 --&gt; n3
  n2 --&gt; n4
  n4 --&gt; n5
```

**One path through the code:** Follow addDocument in FilesService: binary storage is written before metadata. If the second write fails, the first can leave an orphaned file. A production version needs cleanup or another explicit consistency strategy.

## Constraints and checks

Role annotations need the corresponding security configuration. Extension checks are not content validation, and buffering document.bytes loads the upload into memory.

## Files to read

- [src/main/kotlin/com/api/project/controller/FilesController.kt](https://github.com/antoinebou12/SpringBootFilesUploader/blob/main/src/main/kotlin/com/api/project/controller/FilesController.kt)
- [src/main/kotlin/com/api/project/service/FilesService.kt](https://github.com/antoinebou12/SpringBootFilesUploader/blob/main/src/main/kotlin/com/api/project/service/FilesService.kt)
- [build.gradle.kts](https://github.com/antoinebou12/SpringBootFilesUploader/blob/main/build.gradle.kts)

# switch-wifi: Separating network measurements from the UI

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/switch-wifi/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/switch-wifi/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/switch-wifi
- License: MIT
- Inspected revision: 8ff883f6925c37b14b9683f8b933a9403654d08d

## Summary

switch-wifi is a Switch network dashboard with a Borealis interface. It separates portable metric calculations from the console application so that host tests can exercise the core without requiring the Switch toolchain.

**Why it exists:** Native C&#43;&#43; network configuration tool interfacing directly with Switch horizon OS wlan services.

**Best fit:** Fast headless Wi-Fi network credential provisioning on Switch.

## Use cases

Nintendo Switch homebrew app that shows Wi-Fi state, benchmarks the HTTPS path and reads Bluetooth status.

- **Check the Wi-Fi link** (Switch owner, Horizon NIFM / BTM): The Dashboard tab reads link type, SSID, IPv4, gateway, DNS and 0-3 signal bars from NIFM through NetworkService, with RSSI from legacy wlan:inf only where firmware exposes it.
- **Benchmark the connection** (Switch owner, HTTPS speed server): SpeedTestEngine runs 8 HTTPS latency probes, then a 25 MiB download and a 10 MiB zero-filled upload with libcurl against speed.cloudflare.com by default, reporting median, P95 and jitter.
- **Review saved networks** (Switch owner, Horizon NIFM / BTM): The Networks tab lists basic saved-profile metadata and Horizon&#39;s allowed channels, with channel-overlap math from core/metrics; credentials are never read for display.
- **Scan Bluetooth state** (Switch owner, Horizon NIFM / BTM): BluetoothService reads BTM radio state and device counts, and runs a bounded passive BLE scan that returns at most ten unique addresses.
- **Export a diagnostics report** (Switch owner): The About tab writes sdmc:/switch-wifi-diagnostics.txt with the app version, compatibility target, network details and Bluetooth counts, without credentials.

### Scenario: Compare two router channels on a Switch

1. Build build-switch/switch-wifi.nro in the devkitpro/devkita64 container and check it with python3 scripts/verify_nro.py.
2. Copy the NRO to the SD card and launch it from the homebrew menu.
3. Open the Dashboard tab to confirm the Switch is on Wi-Fi and note the signal bars.
4. Run the Benchmark tab and read median latency, P95, jitter, download and upload speed.
5. Change the router channel, run the benchmark again and compare the history graphs.
6. Export sdmc:/switch-wifi-diagnostics.txt from the About tab to keep the result.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| C&#43;&#43; | 86.58 |
| CMake | 8.31 |
| Python | 5.11 |

```bash
cd switch-wifi
```

### README.md · Recommended: official devkitPro container

```bash
docker run --rm \
  -v &#34;$PWD:/work&#34; -w /work \
  devkitpro/devkita64:latest \
  bash -lc &#39;cmake -S . -B build-switch \
    -DPLATFORM_SWITCH=ON \
    -DUSE_GLFW=ON \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release &amp;&amp; \

```


```bash
cmake --build build-switch --target switch-wifi.nro --parallel
```


## Features and components

- **Portable metric core** — CMake creates switch_wifi_core from src/core/metrics.cpp. Host test targets link this library separately from Borealis. Tests cover metrics, history and benchmark behavior, with optional sanitizers.
- **Console integration** — The application target collects the src modules and links Borealis, libnx platform libraries and libcurl. Network activity and the UI therefore depend on platform services, while the numeric core can stay independent.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Network samples → Portable metrics core
- Portable metrics core → History and benchmark results
- History and benchmark results → Borealis dashboard
- Host unit tests → Portable metrics core

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;Network samples&#34;]
  n1[&#34;Portable metrics core&#34;]
  n2[&#34;History and benchmark results&#34;]
  n3[&#34;Borealis dashboard&#34;]
  n4[&#34;Host unit tests&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n2 --&gt; n3
  n4 --&gt; n1
```

**One path through the code:** Start with the core library target and its tests, then inspect the network module feeding its samples. An HTTPS throughput measurement includes the chosen remote server and network path; it is not a direct reading of Wi-Fi radio capacity.

## Constraints and checks

Unavailable radio values should remain unavailable, not appear as zero. Build configuration does not prove support or accuracy on every firmware.

# TCH099: One PHP router for pages and API calls

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/tch099/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/tch099/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/TCH099
- License: MIT
- Inspected revision: a7323c88b2ae6c12d89ef685c6a4cf4325218afc

## Summary

TCH099 is a teaching-oriented web project that combines static frontend pages with PHP API handlers. The route file makes the boundary visible: some paths return HTML files, while others dispatch to server-side scripts.

**Why it exists:** Isolated multi-container environment with bridge networking, MariaDB persistence, and web interfaces.

**Best fit:** Full-stack containerized database application reference.

## Use cases

PHP and MariaDB demo web app with an Android client, used to teach routing, sessions and Azure deployment.

- **Create an account** (Web or mobile user, MariaDB database): The signup page or SignupActivity on Android posts to /api/signup; api/signup.php calls registerUser(), which inserts the account into the Clients table created by db/1create.sql.
- **Log in with a session** (Web or mobile user, MariaDB database): login.html and LoginActivity post the username and password to /api/login; api/login.php checks them with loginUser() and opens a PHP session, and /api/logout closes it.
- **Show a random image** (Web or mobile user): random-image.html calls /api/random-image, which returns a cat picture URL from TheCatAPI or a thispersondoesnotexist.com URL depending on imageType.
- **Get a greeting by language** (Web or mobile user): /api/hello-world/$langue answers with a greeting in French, English, Spanish or German, as a minimal API example.
- **List clients as admin** (Administrator, MariaDB database): The /admin route serves admin.html only when isAdmin() is true; the page loads /api/clients, which reads the Clients table for a session whose role is admin.

### Scenario: Run the demo locally and reach the admin page

1. Fill the DB_HOST and MYSQL_* variables listed in the README, then run docker-compose up -d --build.
2. Load the schema and seed data with python3 db/db.py, or import db/1create.sql, 2contraines.sql and 3insert.sql in phpMyAdmin on port 8060.
3. Open http://localhost:8001/signup, create an account, then log in at /login.
4. With an admin account, open /admin to see the Clients table loaded from /api/clients.
5. Push to main to let .github/workflows/main_tch099antoine.yml zip the app and deploy it to the Azure Web App.

| --- | ---: |

## Features and components

- **Page routes** — routes.php includes router.php, maps the home and login paths to frontend files, and defines 403 and 404 pages. The /admin callback explicitly branches on isAdmin before choosing its response.
- **API handlers** — Login, signup, logout and user_details use individual API scripts. Demonstration routes include a language parameter and random-image responses. Their handlers own request processing; the router only chooses where it goes.

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- PHP router → Frontend HTML page
- PHP router → API handler
- API handler → Application data

```mermaid
  n4[&#34;Application data&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n1 --&gt; n3
  n3 --&gt; n4
```

**One path through the code:** Compare GET /login with POST /api/login. The first selects a page; the second invokes authentication logic. Access checks belong on protected API operations as well as on the administrative page.

# TradingViewBuilder: Pine Script indicators and strategies

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/tradingviewbuilder/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/tradingviewbuilder/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/AlgoETS/TradingViewBuilder
- Inspected revision: 2b5bed6ac9672d4bdb6e3e8e61dc3494dc70edc0


## Use cases

Pine Script indicators and strategies (EMA, MACD, RSI, Bollinger, RVI …) to paste into TradingView.

- **Plot an indicator** (Trader, TradingView): Paste a .indicator file such as rsi.indicator or macd.indicator into the Pine Editor and add it to the chart to plot the series and its levels.
- **Test a crossover strategy** (Trader, TradingView): ema.strategy, mac.strategy and macd.strategy enter on a fast/slow or MACD/signal crossover and reverse or close on the opposite cross.
- **Trade band reversals** (Trader, TradingView): bollingerbands.strategy and linearregression.strategy go long when the close crosses above the lower band and short when it crosses below the upper band.
- **Trade oscillator signals** (Trader, TradingView): rsi.strategy trades RSI crosses of the 30 and 70 levels, and rvi.strategy trades crosses of the Relative Vigor Index and its signal line.
- **Tune script inputs** (Trader, TradingView): Each script declares input() values (lengths, multipliers, levels) that the README says to change from the gear icon on the chart.
- **Sketch a momentum portfolio** (Trader): TimeSeriesMomentumEffect.strategy outlines a 12-month time-series momentum on 60 futures with volatility targeting and a leverage cap; it is a draft, not valid Pine.

### Scenario: Backtest the RSI strategy on a chart

1. Log in to TradingView, open a chart and click the Pine Editor tab.
2. Copy the contents of rsi.strategy and paste it into the editor.
3. Click Add to Chart: Long entries appear when RSI(14) crosses above 30 and Short entries when it crosses below 70.
4. Open the gear icon to change RSI Length, Overbought Level or Oversold Level and compare the trades.
5. Add rsi.indicator in a separate pane to see the oscillator with the same levels.

# TrueMapData: height maps for metrology and graphics

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/truemapdata/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/truemapdata/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/ETSim/TrueMapData
- Inspected revision: 8e44bd4e57ad46eba45c46c997bd6b51d7622956


## Use cases

Python library and tmd-process CLI that read TrueMap and GelSight .tmd height maps for metrology, wear and 3D export.

- **Load a .tmd height map** (Tribology researcher, TrueMap / GelSight): TMD.load(&#34;file.tmd&#34;) in tmd/core/tmd.py decodes v1 or v2 headers and returns height_map as a float32 (height, width) array plus a metadata dict.
- **Export texture maps** (Tribology researcher): tmd-process maps all|normal|ao|bump|hillshade|displacement writes PNG maps through the generators in tmd/image/maps/, and maps batch processes a whole folder.
- **Export a 3D mesh** (Tribology researcher): tmd-process mesh generate exports STL, OBJ, PLY, glTF or USD with adaptive or quadtree triangulation; mesh apply puts the maps on a template OBJ/MTL such as tmd/fixtures/templates/plane.
- **Measure ISO 25178 roughness** (Tribology researcher, Surfalize (ISO 25178)): tmd-process roughness file &lt;path&gt; --quick computes areal parameters through the optional truemapdata[roughness] extra, which installs Surfalize under GPL-3.0.
- **Track wear across scans** (Tribology researcher, TrueMap / GelSight): tmd-wear (same as tmd-process wear) computes bearing curves, wear-volume series, slip axis and scratch evolution on aligned sequences, using tmd/sequence/wear_analysis.py.
- **Plot surfaces and profiles** (Tribology researcher): tmd-process visualize basic &lt;file&gt; draws 2D heatmaps, 3D surfaces and X/Y profiles with the matplotlib, plotly, seaborn or optional Polyscope plotters; tribology plot writes a PNG dashboard.

### Scenario: Compare two GelSight captures of a worn sample

1. Install the package with pip install truemapdata, or pip install -e . from a clone.
2. Run tmd-wear bearing curve examples/gelsight/circle_0mm_100g_heightmap_linear_detrend.tmd --json to get the Abbott curve of the first capture.
3. Run tmd-wear volume-series with that file and tests/fixtures/gelsight_wear_volume_second_frame.tmd to measure the volume lost between frames.
4. Export textures with tmd-process maps all &lt;file&gt; -o ./maps_out.
5. Build a mesh with tmd-process mesh generate &lt;file&gt; --format stl --method adaptive --quality high for a 3D view of the worn area.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| Jupyter Notebook | 94.36 |
| Python | 5.64 |


### README.md · Installation

```bash
pip install &#34;truemapdata[mesh,viz,advanced]&#34;
pip install &#34;truemapdata[roughness]&#34;   # Surfalize (GPL-3.0); Python 3.10&#43; only
```

# uml-mcp: From an MCP tool call to a diagram

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/uml-mcp/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/uml-mcp/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/uml-mcp
- License: MIT
- Inspected revision: ebaeac6eb6737639cd1fd5e92967408309a9a64d

## Summary

uml-mcp exposes diagram tools to MCP clients. The client supplies diagram source and options; the server validates and routes the request to rendering services, then returns diagram results and useful editor links.

**Why it exists:** Flagship Model Context Protocol (MCP) server generating PlantUML, Mermaid, and Kroki directly from LLMs (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT) with zero local dependencies.

**Best fit:** Interactive architectural diagram generation for AI pair programming and automated design docs.

## Use cases

MCP server that lets AI assistants turn diagram source or a description into a rendered diagram inside the chat.

- **Render one diagram** (MCP client (AI chat), Kroki / PlantUML): generate_uml takes a diagram_type, the source code, a format and an optional theme, renders through Kroki (KROKI_SERVER, https://kroki.io by default) and returns the file, its URL and a playground link.
- **Validate diagram source** (MCP client (AI chat)): validate_uml checks the type, format and basic structure locally without rendering, so the assistant can fix the source before calling a renderer.
- **Render a batch of diagrams** (MCP client (AI chat), Kroki / PlantUML): generate_uml_batch renders several items with bounded concurrency and stable ordering, up to the batch_max_items setting.
- **Edit in the chat viewer** (Developer, MCP client (AI chat)): In clients that support MCP Apps, results open in ui://uml-mcp/diagram-viewer, where the user can zoom, edit the source, change theme or format and export SVG, PNG, HTML or PDF.
- **Self-host the server** (Developer, Kroki / PlantUML): uv tool install uml-mcp &amp;&amp; uml-mcp setup installs it locally; docker-compose.yml starts the server on port 8000 with Kroki containers and an opt-in PlantUML fallback profile, and deploy/helm/uml-mcp targets Kubernetes.

### Scenario: Draw a login sequence from Cursor

1. Add the hosted endpoint https://uml-mcp.vercel.app/mcp to the MCP config, as in .cursor/mcp.json.
2. Ask the assistant: &#34;Draw a sequence diagram of a user logging in through an API gateway.&#34;
3. The assistant calls list_diagram_types, writes Mermaid or PlantUML source and checks it with validate_uml.
4. It calls generate_uml_image; the server renders through Kroki and returns an inline PNG with render and playground links.
5. Open the playground link or the MCP App viewer to edit the source and export SVG.





## Features and components

- **A quiet entry point** — server.py delegates startup to mcp_core.core.server. It resolves the mcp object lazily through __getattr__, avoiding server construction and stdout output merely from importing the module. That matters when stdout carries the stdio protocol.
- **Transport and rendering** — The server supports stdio and HTTP entry paths. The core groups tool registration, configuration and Kroki integration. Rendering is a downstream operation: the MCP layer describes tools and carries their inputs and results.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- MCP client → stdio or HTTP transport
- stdio or HTTP transport → FastMCP tools and validation
- FastMCP tools and validation → Kroki renderer
- Kroki renderer → Diagram result and links
- Diagram result and links → MCP client

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;MCP client&#34;]
  n1[&#34;stdio or HTTP transport&#34;]
  n2[&#34;FastMCP tools and validation&#34;]
  n3[&#34;Kroki renderer&#34;]
  n4[&#34;Diagram result and links&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n2 --&gt; n3
  n3 --&gt; n4
  n4 --&gt; n0
```

**One path through the code:** Start at server.py, follow main into mcp_core, then inspect the registered diagram tool before its renderer. A tool invocation supplies structured arguments; it does not make arbitrary prose valid Mermaid or PlantUML.

## API



## Constraints and checks

Remote rendering transmits the diagram source. Validate the renderer endpoint and data policy before using internal architecture or other confidential material.

# uml-skill: Instructions with a small encoding fallback

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/uml-skill/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/uml-skill/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/uml-skill
- License: MIT
- Inspected revision: 05b27cdbe68ea3a9543b8ce8f66586b62194892a

## Summary

uml-skill packages diagram-writing instructions and a small Python helper. It is a skill bundle, not an MCP server or an image-generation model. The helper can produce a Kroki URL from diagram source.

**Why it exists:** Agent skill bundle providing direct tool definitions and prompt guides for diagram generation.

**Best fit:** Drop-in diagram generation capabilities for LLM agent frameworks.

## Use cases

Agent skill (diagramming-uml) that guides AI coding agents to write diagram source and render it via uml-mcp or Kroki.

- **Install the skill** (Developer, AI coding agent): The README lists npx @smithery/cli@latest skill add antoinebou12/uml, or copying the folder into .cursor/skills/diagramming-uml/ so the agent loads SKILL.md.
- **Plan and write diagram code** (AI coding agent): SKILL.md walks the agent through purpose, diagram type, outline and readability rules (about 25 Mermaid or 30 PlantUML nodes, labelled transitions) before it writes source.
- **Pick a diagram_type** (AI coding agent): references/DIAGRAM-TYPES.md maps intents such as sequence, swimlane, ER or architecture to a Kroki diagram_type and Mermaid or PlantUML form, to be confirmed with uml://types.
- **Render through uml-mcp** (AI coding agent, uml-mcp / Kroki): When uml-mcp is connected, the skill tells the agent to call validate_uml then generate_uml or generate_uml_batch and to return the Kroki url and playground link.
- **Build a Kroki URL offline** (Developer, uml-mcp / Kroki): Without MCP, scripts/kroki_url.py compresses the source with zlib, encodes it in base64url and prints a https://kroki.io/&lt;backend&gt;/&lt;format&gt;/... URL.

### Scenario: Get a shareable sequence diagram link

1. Install the skill with npx @smithery/cli@latest skill add antoinebou12/uml.
2. Ask the agent for a sequence diagram of a checkout flow; the skill activates on the diagram request.
3. The agent picks sequence or Mermaid sequenceDiagram from the intent table and writes the source.
4. With uml-mcp connected, it calls validate_uml and generate_uml and replies with the url, the playground link and a copy of the code.
5. Without uml-mcp, run python scripts/kroki_url.py -t mermaid diagram.mmd to get the link.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| Python | 100 |

## Getting started (repository commands, not run here)

### scripts/README.md · Usage

```bash
python kroki_url.py --help
```

### scripts/README.md · Usage

```bash
python kroki_url.py -t mermaid diagram.mmd
python kroki_url.py -t plantuml -f png diagram.puml
```

### scripts/README.md · Usage

```bash
Get-Content diagram.puml -Raw | python kroki_url.py -t plantuml
```

### scripts/README.md · Usage

```bash
cat diagram.puml | python kroki_url.py -t plantuml
```


## Features and components

- **Instruction layer** — SKILL.md describes the workflow and points to diagram references. An agent can use those instructions with available diagram tools. References supply syntax guidance without becoming an application runtime.
- **Encoding helper** — scripts/kroki_url.py uses standard-library compression and encoding to construct a rendering URL. Generating that URL and requesting the rendered image are separate operations.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Diagram request → Skill and syntax references
- Skill and syntax references → Diagram source
- Diagram source → Kroki URL helper
- Kroki URL helper → Rendering endpoint

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;Diagram request&#34;]
  n1[&#34;Skill and syntax references&#34;]
  n2[&#34;Diagram source&#34;]
  n3[&#34;Kroki URL helper&#34;]
  n4[&#34;Rendering endpoint&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n2 --&gt; n3
  n3 --&gt; n4
```

**One path through the code:** Read the encoder to see how source becomes a URL-safe payload. The helper transports the source; syntax validation and visual quality still depend on the diagram language and renderer.

## Constraints and checks

A URL payload is recoverable text, not encryption. The bundle’s instructions do not guarantee that a chosen external renderer is available.

- [README.md](https://github.com/antoinebou12/uml-skill/blob/main/README.md)

# WearBlender: Blender scenes for wear effects

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/wearblender/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/wearblender/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/ETSim/WearBlender
- Inspected revision: 422ce0f0c2cf80045564859171ee26773ea4469f


## Use cases

Blender example scenes for learning how to fake wear with shaders, geometry nodes and painting.

- **Study an edge-wear shader** (Learner or teacher, Blender 4.5): Edge wear.blend builds a worn-edge mask in the shader editor from Bevel and Geometry nodes, a color ramp and a roughness image texture.
- **Study procedural scratches** (Learner or teacher, Blender 4.5): Scratched.blend combines Voronoi and Noise textures, color ramps and Bump nodes on a Suzanne mesh to draw micro-scratches.
- **Rotate a normal map** (Learner or teacher, Blender 4.5): NormalRotation.blend rotates the vectors of an image-based normal map with Vector Rotate and Vector Math nodes.
- **Drive wear from painted data** (Learner or teacher, Blender 4.5): WeightPainting.blend reads a painted attribute through Named Attribute geometry nodes and an Attribute shader node to mix materials.
- **Offset textures with a flowmap** (Learner or teacher, Blender 4.5): flowmap.blend separates and recombines vector components to push texture coordinates along a flow image.
- **Project a camera texture** (Learner or teacher, Blender 4.5): SurfaceCameraProjection.blend has a second camera, a CameraProjectionMaterial with an emission shader and a rigid-body world.

### Scenario: Take apart the edge-wear scene

1. Clone the repository and open Edge wear.blend in Blender 4.5 LTS.
2. Select the plane and open the Shader Editor to follow the Bevel and Geometry nodes into the color ramp.
3. Change the ramp stops and watch the worn edges grow or shrink in the viewport.
4. Open Scratched.blend and compare how Voronoi and Noise textures feed the Bump node.
5. Copy the node setup into your own material as a starting point.

# WearMachine: CAD files for a GelSight wear bench

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/wearmachine/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/wearmachine/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/ETSim/WearMachine
- Inspected revision: beff25e1c78c84d26598153a20afe76fbae6a9b9


## Use cases

CAD, print and drawing files for a small sliding-wear bench whose samples are scanned with a GelSight sensor.

- **Print the bench parts** (Bench builder, 3D printer or cutter): Print/ holds STL files for the rail, rail holder, ski, pusher, separator, bearing holder, motor bracket, lead-screw nut, sample holders and weight holders.
- **Modify parts in CAD** (Bench builder): Raw/ keeps STEP solids of the sample holders, rail parts and most weight holders so dimensions can be changed before printing.
- **Cut flat parts from DXF** (Bench builder, 3D printer or cutter): Drawing/ provides DXF outlines, including a Base plate that exists only as DXF, plus an Inkscape A4 sheet with 16 holes for a mold.
- **Set the normal load** (Bench builder): Weight Holder parts come in 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 and 1000 g versions to press the sample with a chosen load.
- **Hold samples under GelSight** (Bench builder, GelSight scanner): The 30 mm and 40 mm sample holders and a square benchtop holder position worn samples for GelSight capture, as the README describes.

### Scenario: Build the bench and run a loaded sliding test

1. Open Picture/Assembly.png to see the frame with two rails and the crossbar holding five sample holes.
2. Print Rail, Rail_Holder, Rail_Ski, Pusher, Seperator, Holder Berring, nema17bracket_v2 and t8_nut from Print/Rail/.
3. Cut the Base plate from Drawing/Rail/Base.dxf and assemble the rail with a NEMA 17 motor and T8 lead screw.
4. Print the weight holder for the target load, for example Weight Holder 200g.stl, and place it on the sample.
5. After each sliding distance, move the sample to the 30 mm or 40 mm holder and scan it with the GelSight.

# WearSurfacesDatasets: measured wear-surface sequences

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/wearsurfacesdatasets/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/wearsurfacesdatasets/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/ETSim/WearSurfacesDatasets
- Inspected revision: 6841dff6be997b20c0ec288fd1f2f36a9d8bd8fe


## Use cases

Measured wear-surface map sequences (material, grit, load, distance) with Python tools and a WebGPU viewer.

- **Download the map sequences** (Graphics researcher, Git LFS storage): Parquet leaves and WebDataset shards are Git LFS objects, so git lfs pull replaces the pointers under data/parquet and data/shards.
- **Scrub a wear timeline** (Graphics researcher, WebGPU browser): docs/serve_local.py serves docs/index.html, which reads Parquet with parquet-wasm and renders the maps with WebGPU while the user scrubs distance or presses Play.
- **Align a sequence** (Graphics researcher, WebGPU browser): POST /api/align/sequence runs a two-pass SIFT/ECC registration of the normal maps to frame 0, crops the common region and caches PNGs in data/aligned.
- **Interpolate and extrapolate** (Graphics researcher): python -m alignment.bake adds Catmull-Rom midpoints and FFT plus SLERP extrapolated normal maps after the last measured step.
- **Pack Parquet and shards** (Graphics researcher): generate_datasets.py parquet and webdataset turn a wear/ tree of PNG maps into nested Parquet leaves and shard-*.tar files.
- **Extract maps as PNG** (Graphics researcher): read_datasets.py decompress and generate_datasets.py extract write the JPEG bytes stored per map_type back to image files.

### Scenario: Inspect cardboard wear under 200 g

1. Clone the repository, run git lfs pull and pip install -r requirements.txt.
2. Start python docs/serve_local.py and open http://127.0.0.1:8080/docs/index.html.
3. Pick Cartboard / Raw / Normal · S60 · 200 g and click Load sequence.
4. Click Align sequence, then scrub the distance from 0 mm to 2400 mm or press Play.
5. Run python -m alignment.bake --sequence-id cartboard-raw-normal-s60-200g --pack to add interpolated and extrapolated steps.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| Python | 100 |


### README.md · Quick start — WebGPU wear viewer

```bash
python -m alignment.bake --sequence-id cartboard-raw-normal-s60-200g --pack

```



# WearTrailsExperiments: contact-driven wear trails in the browser

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/weartrailsexperiments/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/weartrailsexperiments/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/ETSim/WearTrailsExperiments
- Inspected revision: 065ad38507733d951f35359059dd7d33c809c5b6


## Use cases

Browser experiments that turn rigid-body contact and sliding into wear and flow maps on a ground texture.

- **Slide a body on the ground** (Graphics researcher, Web browser (WebGL), three.js/Ammo.js CDN): docs/index.html loads three.js 0.158 and Ammo.js from a CDN, then main-clean-complete.js drops a cube, sphere, puck, cone, soft cube or custom GLB on a plane with set speed, force and friction.
- **Compare contact bounding boxes** (Graphics researcher, Web browser (WebGL)): docs/js/bounding-box/ fits the contact patch with AABB, PCA-based OBB, rotating-calipers OMBB, KDOP-8 or a hybrid method.
- **Inspect contact field views** (Graphics researcher, Web browser (WebGL)): Eight picture-in-picture canvases show top, bottom and intersection views, tangential velocity, instant traction, accumulated sliding distance and local wear.
- **Accumulate wear on the ground** (Graphics researcher, Web browser (WebGL)): FlowAccumulationManager adds K x traction x velocity into ground buffers and keeps the sliding direction, encoded as HSVA or RGBA.
- **Blend GLB material variants** (Graphics researcher, Web browser (WebGL)): GroundVariantManager loads a GLB ground with material variants and uses accumulated wear as the blend map and flow direction to rotate textures.
- **Export wear maps as PNG** (Graphics researcher, Web browser (WebGL)): Export Wear Map and Save Stamps write the ground canvases to PNG files through a download link.

### Scenario: Record the wear trail of a sliding cube

1. Serve the docs/ folder with python -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000.
2. Choose Cube (subdiv 10), the OBB (PCA-based) algorithm and a friction value, then click Start.
3. Use Pause, Step Frame and Apply Angular Impulse to follow the contact patch in the PiP views.
4. Switch the wear encoding between HSVA (Direction &#43; Wear) and RGBA to read direction and amount.
5. Click Export Wear Map to save the accumulated ground map as a PNG.

# WordsEnigma: A word game across Redwood and Prisma

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/wordsenigma/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/wordsenigma/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/antoinebou12/WordsEnigma
- License: Unlicense
- Inspected revision: a6564499a87c1442c51ea57e5b01f954654e2180

## Summary

WordsEnigma is a fork with separate Redwood web and API workspaces. Its data model links users, languages, word banks, games and individual guesses. GraphQL services translate application operations into Prisma database calls.

**Why it exists:** TypeScript dictionary validation and game solver engine supporting multiple languages and word lengths.

**Best fit:** Algorithmic word game logic and solver heuristics.

## Use cases

RedwoodJS prototype of a multi-language Wordle, with a French word board, GraphQL API and admin CRUD on PostgreSQL.

- **Guess a five-letter word** (Player): The /phil page (MotDuJourPhilPage/App.tsx) gives six tries on a 6×5 grid, rejects words missing from the French list in data/fr.ts and colours letters and keyboard keys; the solution is hard-coded to GRAND.
- **Create an account** (Player): /signup, /login, /forgot-password and /reset-password use Redwood dbAuth (api/src/functions/auth.ts) against the User model with hashed password and salt.
- **Manage words and word banks** (Administrator): Routes under /admin, wrapped in Private roles=&#34;admin&#34;, give scaffolded CRUD pages for users, languages, words, word banks, games, try rows, letters and statistics through the GraphQL SDL services.
- **Seed French words** (Administrator, Online dictionaries): yarn seed runs scripts/seed.ts, which upserts languages and the fr word bank, then fetches definitions from fr.wiktionary.org or le-dictionnaire.com with the cheerio crawler before inserting words.
- **Track games and streaks** (Player): The Prisma schema stores each Game with its TryRow and Letter records and a Statistic row per user (games played, won, lost, streak, average); the data model is in place but the play pages do not write to it yet.

### Scenario: Run the French board locally

1. Start PostgreSQL with docker run --name=db -e POSTGRES_USER=admin -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=admin -p 5432:5432 -d postgres, as in the root README.
2. In WordsEnigma/, run yarn install, then yarn rw prisma migrate dev to apply api/db/migrations.
3. Run yarn seed to load the languages, the fr word bank and the words.
4. Start yarn redwood dev and open http://localhost:8910/phil.
5. Type five letters, press Enter and read the colours until the word is found or the six rows are used.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| TypeScript | 97.12 |
| CSS | 2.22 |
| JavaScript | 0.4 |
| Dockerfile | 0.16 |
| HTML | 0.07 |
| Shell | 0.02 |

## Features and components

- **Data relationships** — schema.prisma uses PostgreSQL. A Game belongs to a user and word, references a word bank, and has try rows. Language records connect words and user settings, so multilingual behavior has a stored data model.
- **Services and persistence** — games.ts exposes list, read, create, update and delete resolvers using db.game. Relation resolvers fetch the associated user, word, bank and guesses. This layer keeps GraphQL operations close to the persistence model.

## Architecture

Components and connections verified in the repository.

- Redwood web UI → GraphQL API
- GraphQL API → Game service resolvers
- Game service resolvers → Prisma client
- Prisma client → PostgreSQL relations

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  n0[&#34;Redwood web UI&#34;]
  n1[&#34;GraphQL API&#34;]
  n2[&#34;Game service resolvers&#34;]
  n3[&#34;Prisma client&#34;]
  n4[&#34;PostgreSQL relations&#34;]
  n0 --&gt; n1
  n1 --&gt; n2
  n2 --&gt; n3
  n3 --&gt; n4
```

**One path through the code:** Follow the game resolver into findUnique, then its relation resolvers into the linked records. These generic CRUD methods do not by themselves explain guess validation or prove that a user can access only their own games.

## Constraints and checks

The manifest targets an older Redwood and Node toolchain. Authorization and game rules need inspection beyond the generated service shape before redeployment.

# Workshop1: Python learning notebooks

- HTML page: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/workshop1/
- Markdown: https://antoineboucher.info/CV/blog/projects/notes/workshop1/index.md

- Repository: https://github.com/AlgoETS/Workshop1
- Inspected revision: 7858d0e73ce4bee9bff9d6cf455118b8a6cef5f1


## Use cases

AlgoÉTS French workshop: Jupyter notebooks from Python basics to APIs, pandas, charts and a 20-day EMA on Apple stock.

- **Set up a Python environment** (Workshop participant, Jupyter or Colab): 0.1_python_environement covers virtualenv, Anaconda and Jupyter Lab; 0.2_jupyter_cloud shows DeepNote and Google Colab, and the README links a Colab copy of the first notebook.
- **Learn Python basics** (Workshop participant, Jupyter or Colab): 1.1_python_basic and 1.2_python_advanced cover variables, control flow, file I/O on monfichier.txt and a small SQLite database (ma_base.db).
- **Call a web API** (Workshop participant, Jupyter or Colab): 2.1_python_api explains REST verbs, status codes, Bearer tokens, API keys and OAuth, with requests and async httpx examples.
- **Clean data with pandas** (Workshop participant): 3.1_python_panda walks through DataFrames, filtering with loc and iloc, missing values, merges, pandas_ta indicators and a polars comparison.
- **Plot an EMA on Apple stock** (Workshop participant, FMP price API): 5.1_project_ema fetches AAPL daily prices from FMP historical-price-full, computes a 20-day EMA with pandas ewm and plots it against the close with Matplotlib; 4.2 adds SMA, RSI and MACD charts.

### Scenario: Follow the workshop up to the EMA project

1. Clone https://github.com/AlgoETS/Workshop1.git and run pip install -r requirements.txt.
2. Start jupyter notebook, or open 1.0-basic/1.1_python_basic.ipynb in Google Colab from the README link.
3. Work through 1.0-basic, 2.0-api and 3.0-data in order.
4. Open 5.0-project/5.1_project_ema.ipynb and replace YOUR_API_KEY with a Financial Modeling Prep key.
5. Run the cells to load AAPL prices into a DataFrame, add EMA_20 and plot the close price with the 20-day EMA.

## Languages (GitHub Linguist bytes)

| Language | % |
| --- | ---: |
| Jupyter Notebook | 100 |
